summary: Registering a Xero OAuth application is a self-serve process that yields immediate API credentials without requiring a developer approval review. However, Xero strictly prohibits using API data to train or fine-tune artificial intelligence models.

difficulty.headline: Self-serve setup provides immediate API credentials, but AI/ML model training on API data is strictly forbidden.

factors.label: No App Review for Standard Integrations
factors.detail: Human approval and app review are only required if you plan to publish your app on the Xero App Store.

evidence.quote: Only required for apps published to the Xero App Store.

factors.label: Strict Prohibition on AI/ML Model Training
factors.detail: Data obtained through Xero APIs cannot be used to train, fine-tune, or build machine learning or AI models.

evidence.quote: The primary update prohibits the use of data obtained through Xero’s APIs to train or contribute to the creation of any AI or machine learning model.

factors.label: Multi-Tenant Context Management
factors.detail: Every API request requires supplying both a valid access token and a specific tenant ID retrieved via the connections endpoint.

evidence.quote: From there, you can make API calls by providing both a valid access token and authorized tenant id with each request.

can_test_before_approval.detail: Developers can build and test immediately using a free Demo Company included with every Xero developer account.

evidence.quote: Developer account includes a demo company for testing.

requirements.label: Xero Developer Account
requirements.detail: A free developer account registered at developer.xero.com.

requirements.label: Valid HTTPS Redirect URI
requirements.detail: A secure HTTPS callback URL (or http://localhost/ for local development).

evidence.quote: Please note that http://127.0.0.1 cannot be used

requirements.label: Application Terms & Privacy Policy
requirements.detail: Legally binding terms of use and privacy policy made available to your users.

evidence.quote: Your apps must include your own legally binding terms of use and privacy policy (your terms) that are available to any user of your apps and our services.

requirements.label: AI/ML Data Usage Compliance
requirements.detail: Compliance with Xero terms restricting API data usage strictly to approved app functionality without feeding AI models.

evidence.quote: The primary update prohibits the use of data obtained through Xero’s APIs to train or contribute to the creation of any AI or machine learning model.

steps.title: Create Xero Developer Account
steps.detail: Sign up for a free developer account on the Xero developer platform.

steps.title: Register OAuth 2.0 Application
steps.detail: Log in to the developer portal ('My Apps'), click 'New app', select integration type, and enter your app details and redirect URIs.
steps.agent_assist: Draft the app name, company URL, and redirect URIs list (e.g., https://yourdomain.com/callback or http://localhost/).

steps.title: Obtain Client Credentials
steps.detail: Navigate to the Configuration tab of your newly created application to retrieve your Client ID and generate a Client Secret.
steps.agent_assist: Provide instructions for securely storing Client ID and Secret in environment variables.

evidence.quote: Navigate to the Configuration tab to retrieve your Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Configure Scopes and OAuth Flow
steps.detail: Set up your OAuth 2.0 authorization URL requesting required granular scopes and include offline_access to receive refresh tokens.
steps.agent_assist: Draft scope parameter strings combining granular scopes (e.g., accounting.invoices) and offline_access for backend token storage.

evidence.quote: Make sure you add the offline_access scope to ensure the token refreshes as expected.

steps.title: Test Integration with Demo Company
steps.detail: Execute the OAuth authorization code flow against Xero's Demo Company, exchange authorization codes for access and refresh tokens, and test API endpoints.
steps.agent_assist: Generate sample OAuth authorization links, build token exchange request handlers, and format API calls passing the xero-tenant-id header.

evidence.quote: Developer account includes a demo company for testing.

gotchas.title: Strict AI/ML Training Ban
gotchas.detail: API data accessed from Xero must never be fed into LLMs or predictive analytics tools for fine-tuning or training.

evidence.quote: The primary update prohibits the use of data obtained through Xero’s APIs to train or contribute to the creation of any AI or machine learning model.

gotchas.title: 30-Minute Access Token Expiration
gotchas.detail: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes; you must request offline_access to get refresh tokens that last up to 60 days.

evidence.quote: However, the access tokens are short-lived, usually expiring after thirty minutes.

gotchas.title: http://127.0.0.1 Unsupported for Redirect URIs
gotchas.detail: Xero permits http://localhost/ for local development callbacks, but explicitly blocks http://127.0.0.1.

evidence.quote: Please note that http://127.0.0.1 cannot be used

gotchas.title: Mandatory Shift to Granular Scopes
gotchas.detail: Broad scopes like accounting.transactions are deprecated in favor of granular scopes like accounting.invoices and accounting.payments.

evidence.quote: Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 will use the new granular scopes

blockers.problem: API returns 401 Forbidden with WWW-Authenticate: insufficient_scope
blockers.why: Your app called an endpoint requiring permissions that were not included when the user authorized your app.
blockers.fix: Add the specific required granular scope to your authorization URL and prompt the user to re-authorize.

evidence.quote: The API will return a 401 forbidden error with a response header WWW-Authenticate:insufficent_scope.

blockers.why: Access tokens automatically expire after 30 minutes.
blockers.fix: Request the offline_access scope during authorization and implement automatic background token refresh using the refresh token.

evidence.quote: However, the access tokens are short-lived, usually expiring after thirty minutes.

blockers.problem: API requests fail due to missing tenant context
blockers.why: Xero requires a valid tenant ID passed in the xero-tenant-id request header for organization endpoints.
blockers.fix: Query GET https://api.xero.com/connections after token exchange to fetch authorized tenant IDs and include the correct tenant ID in subsequent requests.

evidence.quote: Find out which tenants the user has authorized by calling the connections endpoint.

blockers.why: Violating Xero platform terms by using API data for AI model training or deploying automated bots to bypass controls.
blockers.fix: Ensure AI agents handle Xero data purely in memory for user-driven workflows and never retain or send API data into model training datasets.

evidence.quote: If we detect a risk or suspect a breach we may suspend or terminate access to protect the platform.

uncertain: Exact review wait times and process for listing an application publicly on the Xero App Store (no official figure in sources).
